claim_text: The authors connect this to an adipocyte-enriched tumor microenvironment as a plausible source of free fatty acids, but the direct experiments are in cell lines and combination assays rather than patient samples under PI3K-alpha inhibitor selection `pmid-39920872`.
evidence_summary: The paper shows CD36 is high in PTEN-loss anti-HER2-resistant HCC1569 cells, serum deprivation or SSO reduces proliferation, and SSO synergizes with alpelisib/inavolisib; the adipocyte-enriched microenvironment connection is discussed from prior literature, while experiments are cell-line combination assays.
reviewer_notes: The claim accurately separates direct experiments from microenvironmental inference.

claim_text: This supports redox and glycolytic state as a resistance-associated vulnerability, while the exact NAC mechanism remains unresolved `pmid-37044095`.
evidence_summary: NF1 loss in PIK3CA H1047R breast cancer models reduced alpelisib sensitivity, enhanced glycolysis, lowered ROS, and was sensitized by NAC, which reverted glycolysis and dampened mTOR signaling; the discussion states NAC biology and the causal link among mTOR, glycolysis, and synergy remain to be demonstrated.

claim_text: Metabolic imaging work adds a biomarker angle: persistent FOXM1 after PI3K-alpha inhibition was associated with resistance in ER-positive breast cancer models, drove LDHA rather than HK-II, and enabled detection of resistant metabolism by hyperpolarized pyruvate-to-lactate exchange rather than FDG trapping `pmid-32976773`.
evidence_summary: ER-positive PIK3CA-mutant models sensitive to PI3K-alpha inhibition downregulated FOXM1 and LDHA, while resistant or PTEN-altered models maintained FOXM1/LDHA; FOXM1 regulated LDHA but not HK-II, hyperpolarized pyruvate-to-lactate MRI detected response/resistance, and FDG uptake/HK-II measurements were comparatively insensitive.
reviewer_notes: The claim matches the biomarker and imaging distinction in the cited paper.

claim_text: Insulin withdrawal was sufficient to abrogate resistance, and IGF1R or p110beta inhibition circumvented resistance, tying extracellular insulin or IGF input to PI3K-alpha escape but also raising tolerability concerns for dual metabolic-pathway inhibition `pmid-27048245`.
evidence_summary: BYL719-resistant T47D and MCF7 cells showed IGF1R/IRS/p85 phosphorylation and an IGF1R/IRS/p85/p110beta complex; insulin withdrawal abrogated resistance, IGF1R or p110beta inhibitors restored response in vitro and in xenografts, and the discussion warns that PI3K and IGF1R inhibitors can both cause hyperglycemia.
reviewer_notes: Directly supported by mechanistic and tolerability discussion.

claim_text: In patients, the clinical evidence is thinner: a four-patient real-life alpelisib report monitored hyperinsulinemia and used pioglitazone in selected patients, arguing from preclinical evidence that insulin control could preserve efficacy, but without randomized causal testing `pmid-37163178`.
evidence_summary: The report describes four advanced breast cancer patients with insulin monitoring during alpelisib, pioglitazone use for baseline or treatment-emergent hyperinsulinemia/hyperglycemia, and favorable courses; it explicitly relies on animal-model evidence for efficacy rationale and notes the cohort is small and retrospective.
reviewer_notes: No randomized causal test was performed; the claim correctly labels the evidence as thin.

claim_text: CD44-HA interaction in luminal breast cancer models activated Src-ERK and maintained AKT and mTOR activity during alpelisib treatment; hyaluronidase or HAS inhibition partially restored sensitivity, directly linking an extracellular-matrix ligand interaction to reduced PI3K-alpha inhibitor response `pmid-33024087`.
evidence_summary: In luminal PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer models, HA-CD44 signaling activated Src/ERK, sustained AKT/mTOR activity under BYL719, HAS2 expression reduced sensitivity, and hyaluronidase or HAS inhibition rescued BYL719-mediated inhibition and reversed the resistance phenotype.
reviewer_notes: Supported in preclinical luminal breast cancer models.

claim_text: Outside breast cancer, PI3K-pathway inhibitor-resistant lymphoma models upregulated IL-6 and STAT signaling `pmid-31601188`, 3D HNSCC models implicated ECM alterations and beta1 integrin in alpelisib unresponsiveness during radiochemosensitization `pmid-38286037`, and multiple myeloma models showed alpelisib could overcome bone marrow stroma-induced resistance to proteasome-inhibitor contexts `pmid-24405121`.
evidence_summary: PMID 31601188 shows copanlisib- or duvelisib-resistant lymphoma cells upregulate IL-6 and STAT3/5 signaling; PMID 38286037 shows ECM-related mutations enriched in alpelisib non-responder 3D HNSCC models and beta1 integrin targeting improves radiochemosensitization; PMID 24405121 shows BYL719 reduces myeloma adhesion signaling and overcomes bone marrow stroma-induced bortezomib/carfilzomib resistance.
reviewer_notes: The claim is explicitly outside breast cancer and accurately limits the myeloma result to proteasome-inhibitor resistance contexts.
